messages:
From: Connor Taylor <ctaylor@edgescale.ai>

Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing + GPU mix questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the call today — quick follow-up from procurement. EdgeScale runs a mix of long-context embeddings + short-response generation: ~60% steady embedding throughput (~8500 small docs/min), 40% chat/generation spikes (multi-turn, latency-sensitive). We're prototyping on L40S for embeddings but worried about throughput headroom; engineering prefers H100 for latency-critical paths.

We want: a reserved commit that guarantees minimum throughput but lets us burst (pay-as-you-go overage or burst credits). Can you sketch a concrete SKU breakdown (H100 vs A100 vs L40S), how memory reservation would work for large contexts, and what discounts look like for a 12-month commit at 40–60% usage? Also: what SLA do you guarantee for sustained 95th percentile token latency and how does that change across GPU types?

Connor
Procurement Lead, EdgeScale

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing + GPU mix questions

Connor — thanks for the clear breakdown. Putting a short proposal below and attaching a working spreadsheet. We included two packaging routes: throughput-backed commit (tokens/sec guarantees) and capacity-committed GPUs (nodes reserved).

High-level proposal (12-month):
- Split pool (preferred): 70% L40S slab for embedding throughput (cost-efficient, memory-tilted); 30% H100 slab for low-latency gen and KV-heavy contexts.
- Alternate: homogeneous H100 pool with 1.25x reserved capacity for embedding bursts (higher perf/$ for latency but >20% cost increase).
- Throughput guarantee: we can commit to sustained 95th-percentile generation latency target for the H100 slab at your committed throughput; for embeddings slab we guarantee sustained tokens/sec at 99th percentile availability.
- Pricing/discounts: 12-month commit at 40% usage: ~18% discount off list for split pool, 26% for full commit of H100 (reflects larger upfront commitment). Burst credits: includes 10% monthly burst pool; overage billed at pay-as-you-go with priority queueing.

See attached "edgescale_commit_pricing_v2.xlsx" with numbers by GPU type, perf/$, and example monthly cost at 40/60/80% utilization.

Next steps: Kar thik and Ben, can you review the perf assumptions in the sheet and confirm memory/sequence length assumptions for the embedding workload?

— Hannah
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing + GPU mix questions

Posting internal notes into the thread for transparency — Connor, feel free to skip.

Assumptions I used in the workbook:
- Embedding workload: average sequence length 384 tokens, batchable, KV-cache not used. L40S offers ~1.9x perf/$ vs H100 for this profile because of memory bandwidth/packing.
- Generation: avg seq length 64 tokens per request, latency target 95th pct < 120ms. H100 required for <120ms at your concurrency; A100 reaches the target only with aggressive batching which harms p95.
- Memory needs for your long-context feature (60k tokens) will require model sharding or L40S with 80GB variants; we recommend memory-reserved L40S nodes for embedding workers to avoid OOMs.

Operational packaging notes:
- Throughput-backed commit: commit a tokens/sec floor per slab. We translate tokens/sec into a minimum of GPU-minutes/month. This lets you get discounts while we still guarantee perf.
- Burst handling: burst credits are consumed before overage billing; credits refill monthly. Overages auto-scale into hosted capacity at a higher rate but with degraded priority (soft fallbacks possible).

I'll drop updated perf curves into the workbook — Ben, can you add expected concurrency and peak QPS from the EdgeScale sample?

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Connor — added a quick cost/throughput snapshot below pulled from the attached workbook. Numbers are illustrative; final pricing will come from sales ops but this should ground the discussion.

Example monthly (40% commit utilization profile):
- L40S slab (8x 80GB nodes): reserved rate $27k/node-month; effective perf: ~120k embeddings/sec across the slab; perf/$ advantage ~1.9x vs H100 for embeddings.
- H100 slab (3x 80GB nodes): reserved rate $55k/node-month; sustained p95 gen latency <110ms at committed throughput; allows headroom for bursts.
- Combined blended price (split pool 70/30): ~ $250k/month at 40% utilization after 18% commit discount and included burst credits.

Discount flexibility: for a 12-month ramp with quarterly usage guarantees we can move to 22% discount and extend burst credits to 15% if EdgeScale signs a minimum ARR floor (we can put this in a mutual action plan).

Operational caveat: L40S memory variants are in limited supply in some regions; we can earmark capacity on contract signature but lead times vary.

— Ben
Director, Solutions Pricing, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying asks before procurement signs off: 1) Can you contractually commit to the tokens/sec floor mapping to GPU-minutes/month and provide a credits reconciliation report monthly? 2) If L40S lead times push beyond 8 weeks, what fallback do we get to keep throughput guarantees (e.g., temporary H100 overlay with prorated credits)? 3) Final ask on SLA: what crediting model do you use if p95 latency SLO is missed on the H100 slab?

If you can get a short addendum that answers these three points and a revised workbook with the 22% discount ramp option, procurement will route straight to legal.

Connor
Procurement Lead, EdgeScale
